newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL AND BARCELONA WARM UP FOR DECISIVE CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL AND BARCELONA WARM UP FOR DECISIVE CUP CLASH.

text.p: The Spanish league championship is increasingly looking like a two-horse race after a weekend in which Real Madrid and Barcelona warmed up for their forthcoming Cup clash by crushing weaker opponents.

With the nearest challenger now seven points adrift, the pair look to have Spain's two Champions' League places sewn up. But Thursday's fourth round tie could influence the rivals' bid for the league title
"It could have a psychological effect," acknowledged international defender Sergi Barjuan, who scored a fine goal in Barcelona's 6-0 win over Rayo Vallecano.
Ronaldo notched a first-half hat-trick as Bobby Robson's side went on the rampage, but the brilliant Brazilian is doubtful for the Real game after limping off injured on Sunday.
Robson has been criticised by several Spanish commentators for not being quicker to substitute Ronaldo.
The young striker has excelled against weaker sides since signing from PSV Eindhoven in the close season, but has yet to prove himself against the big clubs.
Ronaldo missed Barcelona's 3-3 thriller with champions Atletico Madrid through injury, and was a shadow of himself in last month's 2-0 league defeat at Real's Santiago Bernabeu stadium.
But in the possible absence of Ronaldo, Barcelona have discovered an unlikely new match-winner in the shape of utillity player Luis Enrique Martinez.
Luis Enrique followed up a match-saving hat-trick at Real Betis with yet another header to open the scoring against Rayo.
Raul Gonzalez, his former team mate at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, also kept his goal instinct fine-tuned in Real's 4-0 victory over Celta Vigo.
The victory meant that Real reach the half-way stage of the league on top, achieving what Spaniards call 'the winter championship'.
But Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz rejected any triumphalism.
"It doesn't mean anything if we don't end the season on top," said Sanz, "Although being unbeaten still is very important."
Barcelona will hope to change that state of affairs in Thursday's Cup game in the Camp Nou stadium.
